cohorts.subjects: Cadavers from the Department of Anatomy, Government Medical College and Hospital, Nagpur, India; the title calls them the Indian population (no finer ethnicity given). Excluded: cadavers with obvious deformity of the spine or a fractured spine. Dissected by a midline posterior approach from T12 to the sacrum; the L1-to-sacrum segment was removed and its pedicles L1 to L5 measured. Stature, weight and cause of death not given. The two female cadavers were not compared with earlier studies. The recommendation rows (screw sizes) are drawn from these measurements.
cohorts.n_units: L1 to L5 of 20 cadavers (Inference: 100 vertebrae); whether one or both pedicles of a level were measured is not stated
cohorts.ages: males 20 to 70 years; the two females 55 and 60 years

techniques.instrument: Vernier caliper (resolution 0.1 mm) for distances, goniometer (resolution 1 deg) for angles, on the dissected cadaver column (not stated to be macerated dry bone)
techniques.how: First, on the intact L1 to L5 column: interpedicular distance, sagittal diameter (pedicle height, Figure 2 draws it across the pedicle between the notches) and sagittal angle (one line along the pedicle axis, one along the superior border of the body, after Olsewski; positive cephalad, negative caudad). The interpedicular distance is not defined in words; Inference from p. 456 and p. 458: between pedicles of adjacent vertebrae, L1 standing for L1-L2.

techniques.instrument: roentgenograms of the excised column; goniometer (1 deg) for the angles; distances presumably with the Vernier caliper, since all diameters and distances were (Inference)
techniques.how: Roentgenograms of the vertebral column for sagittal diameter, sagittal angle and interpedicular distance, taken after the direct measurements; the angles were read on lateral roentgenograms; the projection for the two distances is not stated (Inference: lateral, since the authors blame overlap of left and right pedicles for the larger radiographic interpedicular distance).
techniques.magnification: tube to cassette 100 cm (printed as about 33 inches); a metal measuring guide gave a magnifying factor reported as 0, so no correction is described

techniques.instrument: CT (called computerized roentgenogram), scanner not named; hard-copy films read with computer software for distances and a goniometer for angles
techniques.how: 5-mm-thick axial slices cut at the pedicle isthmus (midpedicle cut), the plane chosen on the sagittal view; transverse diameter, transverse angle, chord length and medial and lateral cortical thickness measured on the films. Whether the excised segment or the whole cadaver was scanned is not stated.
techniques.magnification: not stated (lengths read with software from the films)

techniques.instrument: oscillating fret hacksaw; Vernier caliper (0.1 mm) and goniometer (1 deg)
techniques.how: Vertebrae cut at the midpedicle level after CT; transverse diameter (mediolateral width at the narrowest part, Figure 1), transverse angle (pedicle axis against the midline, Figure 1) and chord length (labelled along the pedicle axis in Figure 1; posterior start not defined) measured on the cut surface.

In the lateral plane the pedicle centre was placed against the transverse process (top, upper half, midpoint or lower half) and against the superior facet divided by vertical lines into segments 1 to 4, the fourth lateral to the facet (Figure 3).

within_paper: One set of subjects for all this paper's own values: the same 20 cadavers' L1 to L5 were measured four ways in sequence, directly on the intact column (interpedicular distance, sagittal diameter, sagittal angle), on roentgenograms (the same three), on CT (transverse diameter, transverse angle, chord length, cortical thickness) and directly after sawing at midpedicle (transverse diameter, transverse angle, chord length, entrance point), pp. 453-454 (PDF 1-2). So each Direct row and its Roentgenogram or CT row in Tables 1 and 2 are the same pedicles by two methods. The M(18) and F(2) rows split the 20 cadavers; the cortical thickness rows name no sex (Inference: all 20). The values in the Abstract, Results and Discussion repeat table values. Of the comparators, the Olsewski rows (M(24), F(25), (51), (49)) all come from one study, olsewski1990 (Inference: Part 1 cadavers and Part 2 radiographs), and the Zindrick (85) rows of both tables from one.
